title: Aniimo Collection Badges And Aniilog Research Explained | Full Collecting Guide | Aniimo Guide
description: How Collection Badges and Aniilog research work in Aniimo: the four badge tiers and their requirements, how to check progress on the map, the Bronze catch bonus, and how research unlocks accessory slots.

sections.heading: Two collection systems in one game
sections.script: Aniimo gives you two different ways to show off how much of the world you have seen. One is the Collection Badge, which belongs to a whole region. The other is Aniilog research, which belongs to a single creature. They share the same tier names, Bronze, Silver, Gold and Prismatic, and that is exactly why players mix them up. In this video we separate them. We explain what each badge tier asks for, how to check your progress on the map, what the Bronze badge gives you, and then how Aniilog research unlocks accessory slots. We already covered the big picture in our roadmap video, so here we go deeper on collecting. As always, these guides are fan written and patches change things, so check the requirements shown in your game.

sections.heading: What a Collection Badge is
sections.script: Let us start with the badges. A Collection Badge is a marker of your exploration progress in one region. Guides describe it as trophy like, and not an item you can use, but it still matters because it feeds your progression and gives regional buffs in the matching area. Every region has four badge levels. You begin by catching the native Aniimo of the region, which earns the lowest badge. Notice the word native. The percentage counts the creatures that belong to that region, so a creature you already caught elsewhere may still need to be caught again in each area where it appears. That small detail trips up many players, and it explains why a region sometimes feels stuck at ninety nine percent.

sections.heading: Bronze, Silver, Gold and Prismatic
sections.script: Here are the four tiers, and the guides agree on them. Bronze asks for forty percent collection progress in the region. Silver asks for seventy percent, and you must also defeat the local Alpha Aniimo. Gold asks for one hundred percent progress, and you must obtain five Lumin Amber in the region. Prismatic is the hardest. You need to own the specific Sparkling Prismana of that region, and you also need to reach the Prismatic tier of research for a particular Aniimo. One guide uses the name Glowing Amber for the Gold item, but it is the same goal. Notice how each step adds a new kind of task. Bronze is about catching, Silver adds a boss, Gold adds exploration for Lumin Amber, and Prismatic adds a rare variant.

sections.heading: How to check what you need
sections.script: You never have to guess your requirements. Open the map and select the region you care about. Click one of your unlocked fast travel points, and if you have none yet, visit the region and interact with one first. You will see a Collection Badge icon near the bottom right of the screen. Open it and you can browse all four badge levels and read what each one needs. A progress bar in the same window shows your overall collection percentage, but it only shows the catching part. The other goals, like the Alpha or the Lumin Amber, are listed on the requirements page. So check both before you plan your route. It takes only a minute, and it saves you from wandering around a region for no reason.

sections.heading: The Bronze badge in practice
sections.script: Let us look at one real example, the Bronze badge for Forest of Falling Stars in the Breezy Plains region. It asks for forty percent collection progress and nothing else, no boss and no Lumin Amber. According to one guide, you catch new species in the open fields, and only new species count toward the bar. When you pass the threshold, a banner tells you the badge is obtained. And the reward is useful. Guides say the Bronze badge gives a ten percent boost to your catch chance in that area, and it also lets you use Nurture there. A second Bronze badge guide, for Beast Fang Ridge, lists the same two perks. So the early badges help you catch the rest of the region faster.

sections.heading: Catching tips for collection
sections.script: Catching is the heart of the first tier, so a few tips help. Guides say full health Aniimo often break free from a pod, so weaken your target first before you throw. For stubborn species, one guide suggests using an ultimate skill before the throw. Keep track of what is still missing in the Aniilog, and plan a loop through the region instead of running back and forth. Every new catch helps your regional percentage, so one habit feeds the other.

sections.heading: Badges and experience
sections.script: Why bother with badges at all? One reason is experience. Guides say Bronze and Silver badges feed Safaris EXP, which is your character experience which is your character experience. You may also need to claim the reward by hand, so look for it on the world map. The badges also appear as goals in Elite Training. For example, the Bronze badge for Beast Fang Ridge is listed as one of the core courses in a chapter two course, and the Forest of Falling Stars badge can be tracked under the first steps with Aniimo. Because of this, collecting along your story route fills two bars at once.

sections.heading: Aniilog research levels
sections.script: Now the second system, Aniilog research. Every creature has an entry in your Aniilog, and each entry has four research levels called Bronze, Silver, Gold and Prismatic. Guides explain that these levels unlock accessory slots, two slots at Bronze, three at Silver, four at Gold and five at Prismatic. The slots stack, so the maximum is five. You earn research points from two places inside the entry. Field Notes are discoveries, for example photographing the exact Aniimo or clearing certain Sanctums. Topics are tasks in the Topic menu and finishing milestones there adds points too.

sections.heading: Using your new accessory slots
sections.script: When you reach a new research tier, the game shows a message saying that an accessory slot is unlocked, and the research crown on the entry updates. Nothing is equipped automatically, so you have to do that part yourself. Open Appearance, go to the Aniimo tab, select the new slot and choose an accessory you own. One detail is worth remembering. The accessories belong to the individual creature wearing them. And a warning for collectors. Prismatic research does not give you a Prismana form or the Sparkling trait. Those are separate collection systems that you still have to chase.

sections.heading: A simple collecting plan
sections.script: Here is an easy plan that guides support. First, claim every Bronze badge you can along the story, because the catch bonus helps the next steps. Second, check each region's requirements page, and write down which Alpha you need for Silver. Third, collect Lumin Amber as you explore, because Gold needs five in the region. Fourth, keep a short list of creatures you want to research, and photograph or complete Field Notes when you meet them. Do not try to finish everything at once. Collecting is a long goal, and the game rewards steady progress. One region at a time, and a few Aniilog entries on the side, is more than enough.

sections.heading: Which badge are you chasing
sections.script: That is our guide to collection in Aniimo. Remember the two systems. Region badges ask for forty percent, seventy percent with an Alpha, one hundred percent with five Lumin Amber, and a Sparkling Prismana. Aniilog research gives creatures up to five accessory slots. Now it is your turn. Which region badge are you chasing right now, and which one is giving you the most trouble? Tell us in the comments, and your answer might help another Pathfinder.
